UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S MOTION UNDER RULE 26(d)(1) FOR PRESENT AUTHORIZATION TO SERVE TWO INTERROGATORIES ON META CONCERNING PLAINTIFF’S FULL LEGAL NAME AND FACEBOOK ACCOUNT

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1) for an order authorizing him to serve two interrogatories, in the form attached as Exhibit A (“Exhibit A — Meta — November 7, 2026 — Final”), on Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) before the Rule 26(f) conference. Plaintiff asks for that authorization as an express, limited exception to the discovery posture described in ECF No. 108 and notwithstanding the denial of Plaintiff’s earlier requests in ECF No. 84. A Memorandum in Support, the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine with Declaration Exhibit 1, a Proposed Order, an Alternative Referral Order, and a Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument and Request for Prompt Determination on the Papers accompany this Motion. Plaintiff incorporates the Memorandum by reference.

I.	THE RELIEF REQUESTED

1.	Meta is the sole discovery respondent. Exhibit A asks two questions. Interrogatory No. 1 asks whether Meta submitted to NCMEC, between July 1, 2022 and April 22, 2026, inclusive, any CyberTipline report that, as submitted by Meta, contained or otherwise identified the full legal name “Marvelle J. Ballentine.” Interrogatory No. 2 asks whether Meta submitted to NCMEC, in the same inclusive period, any CyberTipline report in connection with the Facebook account associated with Plaintiff and enforced against on or about July 4, 2022. The permitted answers to each interrogatory are “Yes,” “No,” or “Unable to determine after reasonable inquiry,” with a qualification confined to what accuracy requires. Exhibit A requests no report, no report number, no report date, no submitter identity, and no narrative.

2.	The two interrogatories are independent. Neither answer is conditioned on the other. This application does not await any answer from NCMEC. No interrogatory is directed to any other Defendant.

3.	This is a present application with a changed scope. The request denied in ECF No. 84 (ECF No. 54) asked four questions, including alias and email questions with a conditional-answer design. Exhibit A asks two independent questions. The full-name question reaches any qualifying report Meta submitted within the stated period, not only the two reports the letters describe or the specified account. The account question addresses the inquiry Meta’s own memorandum describes. ECF No. 22 at 4, 6. The alias and email questions are no longer requested. The full-name subject appeared in the earlier request.

4.	Plaintiff asks for an express, limited exception to the posture stated in ECF No. 108 at 2. This Motion seeks no reconsideration or vacatur of ECF No. 84 or ECF No. 108. The objections and revision requests pending at ECF Nos. 89, 93, 112–113, and 118–123 remain pending and are not affected by this Motion.

II.	THE GROUNDS

5.	The association between Plaintiff’s full legal name and two CyberTipline reports is in the public litigation record. ECF No. 7-2 at 2, 14, 16; ECF No. 7-5 at 2–3. Meta describes the letters as the exact discovery of whether Meta reported and has not stated what it submitted. ECF No. 22 at 4, 9, 11. Plaintiff has never seen a CyberTipline report and does not know whether any original report contains his full legal name. Ballentine Decl. ¶¶ 5–6. The Declaration describes the present consequences of that unresolved association for Plaintiff’s decision to retain counsel, his professional participation, and his daily work and family responsibilities. Id. ¶¶ 8–16.

6.	Ordinary discovery is deferred until the pending motions to dismiss are resolved. ECF No. 108 at 2. Meta requests dismissal with prejudice and proposes discovery only after the claims survive. ECF No. 22 at 14; ECF No. 73 at 4. That sequence risks ending ordinary discovery in this action before Plaintiff receives either answer requested.

7.	The Memorandum develops two grounds. First, Plaintiff asks the Court to apply the modified preliminary-injunction framework stated in Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. v. Markfeld, No. 3:25-cv-00885-RCY, ECF No. 70 at 17–18 (E.D. Va. July 29, 2026), and Shenzhenshibairihongmaoyiyouxiangongsi v. Novoluto GmbH, No. 3:25-cv-00844-RCY, ECF No. 44 at 3–6 (E.D. Va. Mar. 9, 2026), and submits that the record satisfies it. Mem. Parts VIII.A–VIII.F. Second, Plaintiff submits that good cause independently supports this limited authorization. Strike 3 Holdings, LLC v. Doe, No. 1:25-cv-01308-MSN-WBP, ECF No. 7 at 1–3 (E.D. Va. Aug. 21, 2025). Mem. Part VIII.G.

III.	ROUTING, SUBMISSION, AND TIMING

8.	ECF No. 108 at 2 attributes the deferral of discovery to the District Judge’s choice. Plaintiff asks the District Judge to determine this application. If the District Judge refers it, Plaintiff asks that the referral expressly authorize determination of the limited exception under Rule 26(d)(1), including its timing and any response period. If the application is before the Magistrate Judge and he regards the deferral as reserving the question, Plaintiff asks that he state that understanding and present the limited-exception request to the District Judge.

9.	Plaintiff waives oral argument and requests prompt determination upon completion of briefing, subject to the Court’s directions. To the extent an adverse disposition would depend on the specific reporting fact addressed by Exhibit A, Plaintiff requests that the Court resolve this authorization request before or expressly within that disposition. Plaintiff requests no general stay and no deferral of any dismissal ruling.

10.	Plaintiff asks that the order require him to serve Exhibit A within three days after entry, and require Meta to serve its answers and any objections within seven days after that service, or within a definite period the Court fixes. The answers should be made through an officer or agent furnishing the information available to the organization under Rule 33(b)(1)(B), under oath under Rule 33(b)(3), with any objection stated with specificity under Rule 33(b)(4), and signed as Rule 33(b)(5) requires.

IV.	LOCAL CIVIL RULE 37(E) STATEMENT

11.	[Complete from the telephone conference or documented attempts with counsel for Meta. State: the date and Eastern time; the means (telephone or in person); the participants; that Plaintiff presented the two Exhibit A questions in their exact form and requested voluntary answers; the request for the seven-day response period; counsel’s stated position on search capability by full name and by the specified account, additional steps, time, and any burden, privilege, or confidentiality ground; counsel’s position on the modified-test and good-cause standards; counsel’s position on waiver of oral argument and prompt determination on the papers; and each point left unresolved. If counsel did not participate, state each attempt by date, time, and means, and state that no consultation occurred. State agreement only where counsel expressed it. The same account appears at Ballentine Decl. ¶¶ 19–21.]

V.	PRAYER

12.	Plaintiff requests that the Court enter the accompanying Proposed Order, which:

(a)	authorizes Plaintiff to serve on Meta, before the Rule 26(f) conference, the two interrogatories attached as “Exhibit A — Meta — November 7, 2026 — Final,” as an express, limited exception to the discovery posture described in ECF No. 108 and notwithstanding ECF No. 84, and authorizes no other discovery;

(b)	requires Plaintiff to serve Exhibit A within three days after entry;

(c)	requires Meta to serve its answers and any objections within seven days after that service, or within a definite period the Court fixes;

(d)	requires organizational inquiry, answers under oath, specific objections, and signatures under Rule 33(b), subject to the form and content limits stated in Exhibit A;

(e)	authorizes no production of any CyberTipline report and no automatic filing of responses, and reserves the procedures governing later use of the answers, including Rule 12(d) and any applicable confidentiality or sealing requirement;

(f)	deems no answer an admission of liability or a basis for dismissal;

(g)	authorizes no ex parte or in camera submission of any CyberTipline report or related material, and requires that any such submission be served on Plaintiff, subject to any protective order the Court enters;

(h)	supplies the defined prospective relief without adjudicating the matters pending at ECF Nos. 89, 93, 112–113, and 118–123; and

(i)	records the Court’s consideration of Plaintiff’s request for prompt determination on the papers and of the sequencing request stated in paragraph 9.

13.	Alternatively, if the District Judge refers this application, Plaintiff requests entry of the accompanying Alternative Referral Order, which expressly authorizes determination of the limited exception under Rule 26(d)(1), including its timing and any response period.
